callout: On job 50837 the copilot went quiet after the first hour. It woke on schedule five times between 3am and 7am and sent nothing at all — no patrol report asked for, no check on the guard, all the way to the end of the shift.

verdict.summary: The historical baseline and old replay reproduce complete silence across all five scheduled check-ins. The candidate no longer remains quiet: it sends messages on four of five turns, continues through the final 07:00 turn, and explicitly asks the guard for an all-clear or brief patrol update.

criteria.claim: The Copilot must not remain entirely silent across the five scheduled check-ins from 03:00 through 07:00.
The Copilot must check on the guard or request a patrol/status report before the shift ends.
The Copilot must continue communicating through the final scheduled check-in rather than going quiet through the end of the shift.

limitations: Copilot model configurations differ between the old recorded-shift trace and the candidate replay, reducing direct comparability.
Full replay context parity could not be independently verified because one or both replay responses omit debug context.
No guard replies are present, so the evidence establishes that messages and a status/report request were sent, but not how a real guard would respond.
